title: Data Preparation
subtitle: Cleaning, normalising, handling missing values and outliers

content.text: Garbage in, garbage out. Most ML time is spent cleaning and transforming data, not training models.

content.code:
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer

df = pd.read_csv("data.csv")

# Drop duplicates
df = df.drop_duplicates()

# Fill missing values with column median
imp = SimpleImputer(strategy="median")
df[["age","income"]] = imp.fit_transform(df[["age","income"]])

# Standardise features (mean=0, std=1)
scaler = StandardScaler()
X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(df[["age","income"]])

content.text: Always fit the scaler on training data only, then transform both train and test sets.

questions.question: Why should you fit a scaler on training data only?
options: To prevent data leakage from the test set into training
Scalers only work on small datasets
Test data should not be scaled
questions.explanation: Fitting on the whole dataset leaks test-set statistics into training, giving overly optimistic results.

faq.q: Should I remove all rows with missing values?
faq.a: Only if the fraction is small. Otherwise impute (fill in) missing values using the median, mean, or a model.
